legend.0: No defined user decision or business output.
legend.1: A defined user and plausible task exist; evidence is limited to examples and assumptions.
legend.2: A working end-to-end task has independently reviewed synthetic outcomes; no representative user trial measures value.
legend.3: Representative users measured improved task outcomes against their current process, including regressions and review effort.
legend.4: Repeated representative deployments show sustained measured benefits with named owners and monitored regressions.

legend.0: Known failures can silently produce incorrect authoritative decisions.
legend.1: Only happy-path examples are demonstrated; important business invariants are unchecked.
legend.2: Business invariants and failure states have automated tests plus reviewed model outputs; representative domain coverage remains missing.
legend.3: Independent domain-labeled representative cases and adversarial cases meet predeclared error tolerances; regressions are enforced.
legend.4: Production outcomes and change evaluations confirm those tolerances over time, including uncommon and high-impact cases.

legend.0: No runnable setup or usable input/output contract.
legend.1: A developer can run a canned example but an operator cannot follow a documented real-data path.
legend.2: Documented installation, validated file contracts and usable output enable a manual export/import trial; live source integration is unverified.
legend.3: An authorized source adapter and operator journey are tested against a representative sandbox with identity, provenance and freshness preserved.
legend.4: Operators have repeatedly completed onboarding, error recovery and routine use in target environments with maintained connectors.

legend.0: Routine errors can be hidden as success or cause uncontrolled execution.
legend.1: Failures are visible but resource bounds or failure recovery tests are missing.
legend.2: Bounded requests, explicit failures and transport tests exist; sustained workload, restart recovery or operational observation remain unverified.
legend.3: Deployment-specific load, fault, timeout, restart and recovery tests meet declared service objectives with actionable telemetry.
legend.4: An operated service meets recorded objectives over time with tested rollback, recovery drills and accountable incident ownership.

legend.0: Known exploitable critical access or data disclosure defect is unresolved.
legend.1: Controls are mostly stated in documentation; implemented trust boundaries are not tested.
legend.2: Implemented local/provider trust boundaries are tested and deployment exclusions explicit; target identity, authorization and data-governance validation are missing.
legend.3: Target identity and authorization boundaries, retention, secrets and provider approval are independently tested in the intended environment.
legend.4: Ongoing security ownership, vulnerability handling and recurring tests demonstrate those deployment controls remain effective.

legend.0: Untraceable generated assertions are presented as completed business actions.
legend.1: Output requests human review but lacks usable links to the evidence or execution.
legend.2: Output records evidence and execution provenance with explicit uncertainty; review decisions and freshness invalidation are not durably enforced.
legend.3: Review decisions are bound to the exact work product and source versions, durably recorded, and invalidated on changed or ineligible evidence; the stated reviewer identity boundary is enforced.
legend.4: The review lifecycle and authorized source freshness are verified end-to-end in the target business system, including audit retrieval and revocation.

legend.0: Only names, styling or branding distinguish a copied generic demonstration.
legend.1: A repository-specific design or constraint is described but its practical improvement is not demonstrated.
legend.2: A concrete repository-specific capability solves a documented gap and has tests; equivalent upstream or manual baselines have not been executed comparatively.
legend.3: A reproducible comparison against a relevant existing alternative demonstrates a useful improvement and honestly reports tradeoffs.
legend.4: Independent adopters reproduce the comparative improvement on representative tasks and the capability remains maintained.

legend.0: Known required attribution is removed or fabricated ownership, deployments or results are claimed.
legend.1: Origin or maturity statements are ambiguous and supporting artifacts are absent.
legend.2: Origin, implementation scope and limits are stated with linked code and test artifacts; some material claims remain unverified.
legend.3: Material implementation and evaluation claims are traceable, limitations explicit, and applicable source notices retained; no evidence of fabricated claims.
legend.4: Independent provenance and claim audit verifies all material claims and required notices against reproducible records.
